_readme: Letta Code's protocol_v2 App Server runs through `letta server --listen`. These tables hold wire values that the Go provider and TypeScript plugin both read. The Worker stores native `stream_delta` payloads. It stores one payload in the native shape per tool call when a message contains several calls. The plugin reads the same `message_type` and `deltaFields`. `commands` lists client command kinds. `messages` lists server message kinds. `deltaKinds` lists stream message types. `tools` lists native tool names both sides use. The Worker opens subagent rows for `Agent`, answers `AskUserQuestion`, and streams `Bash` output. The plugin draws each tool. `subagentStates` lists child lifecycle values. `loopStatuses` lists busy-state values. Letta owns these values except `modes` and `reply`. LeapMux owns `modes`, which maps permission choices to `runtime_start.mode`. LeapMux owns `reply`, the flat browser decision fields. `kind`, `request_id`, and `decision` stay at the top level, never under `response`.
